title: Attendance and the P grade
summary: The 75% attendance rule and everything a P grade affects.

posts.md:
## When do you get a P?

Students are expected to maintain **100% attendance**, especially because IITM is a residential institute and academics is the core activity.

However, a minimum of **75% attendance** is required to avoid a **P (Poor Attendance)** grade.

The 25% flexibility is intended to accommodate situations such as:

- Short-term medical requirements
- Family functions
- Off-campus interviews
- Exams
- Other genuine requirements

>  The 75% attendance should not be treated as the target. Students are expected to attend classes regularly.

## Keep Track of Your Attendance

IITM uses an app-based attendance management system that allows students to keep track of their attendance.

Make sure you monitor your attendance regularly.

## Consequences of a P Grade

### POR

Students with a **P grade are excluded from applying for PORs**.

### Supplementary Examination

If you have a **P attendance code in a course**, you **cannot apply for the supplementary examination for that course**.

### Minor

If you have a **P grade in any course belonging to your Minor stream**, you **cannot claim the Minor**.

>  **Exception:** Students in their **final semester** can still claim the Minor even if they have a P in a course belonging to the Minor stream.

### Attendance as Class Participation

Faculty may choose to **incentivize attendance through marks/class participation**.

### Parent Alert

Parents may be **alerted if a student's attendance is poor**.

## Additional Rules for P Grades

### SEAT Elective Allotment

Students with **no P grades** will be considered first for elective allotment in SEAT.

Then students will be considered based on the number of P grades:

**0 P → 1 P → 2 P → 3 P → ...**

The SEAT rule uses a **rolling 1-year window**.

This means students are encouraged to improve their attendance over time.

### IDDD Allotment

Students with **no P grades** will be considered first during IDDD allotment.

Those with **1 P** will be considered after them, followed by those with 2 P, 3 P, and so on.

For IDDD allotment, **all attendance data collected up to that point** will be considered.

### 3 or More P Grades

Students with **more than 3 P grades during their tenure at IITM** will not be eligible for consideration for:

IDDD upgradation
Dual Degree upgradation
MSc/MTech → PhD upgradation
YRF
Honours

### Remember

A P grade can affect your **exams, POR eligibility, Minor, elective allotment, and eligibility for certain academic opportunities**.

So, keep track of your attendance and attend classes regularly.
